Its paragraph beginning “Checks at 46e09ffde115d8d44088053a456ba97eff0e694d (local-checks.txt)” attributes the entire listed check set to the new head. That attachment is byte-identical to the previous artifact's local-checks.txt, explicitly headed f09a9b3250c6b28cb4e9aef7738a55955a969222, with SHA-256 5290b2cc76f2683531430401839ecb147675c8fba4756ded55c86c66db5ee374. The fresh request separately says ciguard and reporter tests were rerun at 46e09ffd. Record which checks were actually rerun and which are carried from unchanged source. I requested this clarification in ephemeral chat and have not received it; the durable finding now makes the required correction explicit.

No workflow change, new head, new failing CI fixture or full gate rerun is requested. On the existing implementation commitment, publish a corrected artifact for the same exact head with accurate evidence provenance, cite this finding, retire the replaced artifact as its author, and request fresh independent review. The existing signed logs and independently verified fixture remain useful evidence at their actual execution heads.

Architecture: CI automation only; none of the seven runtime layers in docs/reference/architecture.md changes its contract. The five-line comment accurately describes selection, a running step with no files, and loss of the runner. No architecture-page amendment is required for this correction.

Security: the pinned upload action, read-only permissions, failure predicate, exact two-file selector, warning policy and 30-day retention remain unchanged. No hidden-file opt-in, broad upload, new credential exposure or unresolved source security defect was found. The governing request preserves the historical closing act and recovers its existing retention outcome; it does not introduce new authority or retention policy. The remaining issue is fidelity of the durable evidence record.

Simplification: the revised comment resolves the previous 18-line explanation finding. Keep the narrow implementation intact. Correct the report's attribution directly, without new fixtures, policy machinery or duplicated tests merely to relabel old execution.

Validation: gs review --prepare accepted the exact clean checkout and artifact; HEAD and cleanliness were checked again before this verdict. Every non-comment/nonblank workflow line matches f09a9b32, and ci.yml is the sole changed path. Ten of eleven signed attachments are byte-identical to the previously fully read evidence; the updated workflow diff was read in full. The prior independently executed ciguard/reporter and surface/link/performance checks, pinned-action source inspection, and independent download/hash/retention/fixture-cleanup verification therefore carry as previously dated evidence on unchanged implementation. They were not rerun at 46 or relabeled as new execution. The source correction is satisfactory; approval awaits only an accurate implementation report.

scale_review.text:
Changes requested at exact cbc3b81bd77424e6b141856264af7432c8a3c4f4, all 17 cited paths, against #21875 and assigned implementation #20084. These corrections belong on Claude's existing implementation commitment; this verdict does not withdraw or close that implementation.

1. Reject an empty campaign before creating passing evidence. At cmd/gitseq-perf/main.go:264 the selected case list can be empty, and line 287 initializes outcome to pass without a nonempty check. I ran `go run ./cmd/gitseq-perf run --tier envelope --output /tmp/git21875-empty-envelope-evidence` in the clean exact-head checkout. The default v2 contract has no envelope cells; the command exited 0 and printed `pass: wrote /tmp/git21875-empty-envelope-evidence (0 primary samples)`, with outcome pass in evidence.json. Refuse this unsupported contract/tier combination clearly, and cover the actual lane entry boundary so selecting zero cases cannot silently become a successful campaign. This needs no large timing rerun.

2. Correct the measured environment attribution. docs/reference/performance.md:62-66 says every measured table cell used Go 1.27.0 at the current campaign. The carried fan-out and one-actor memory results used Go 1.26.5, as their retained evidence environment fields and the same page's historical sections say. Scope the Go 1.27.0/head 0b689fe2 statement to this campaign, and retain the historical head/toolchain associations for carried results.

3. Establish or honestly qualify the chronology. #20084 condition 1 requires publishing the versioned target table in the working document before new timing. The measured 0b689fe2 changes only the harness; the table and classification-rules.md first appear in the later publishing commit in the supplied Git record. The signed window notice and campaign/gates attachments I examined do not establish an earlier published table. Retaining a rules file after a run also does not by itself prove its bands were fixed first, as performance/README.md:140-143 claims. I asked ephemerally for author-signed pre-run table/rules evidence and have not received it. Supply the actual durable pre-run basis if one exists; otherwise state the actual chronology, remove unsupported pre-registration claims, and obtain the requester's disposition of the unmet before-timing condition. This is an evidence gap, not a claim that no private earlier draft existed. Do not retrieve private terminal/session transcripts, manufacture retrospective pre-registration, or repeat the large campaign automatically.

4. Correct validation attribution. In the signed mutants-harness.txt, the case `envelope cell duplicates cases the depth axis already carries` failed to compile because the slices import became unused. That does not show TestEnvelopeCellsAddOnlyTheirOwnJointCases rejecting a compiled behavioral defect. Repair and run that mutant, or accurately distinguish compilation failure from a killed behavioral mutant instead of claiming all 28 fail their named tests. The supplied gates-docs.txt identifies head 0b689fe2 and a subsequent commit 0298694e, not final cbc3b81b; do not relabel that log as gates on the final head. Attach correctly attributed final checks with the corrected artifact. My independent checks below establish only the checks I actually ran.

Architecture: the affected Layer 7 command composes the existing Layer 1 Git reads and existing kernel, application-host and projection scenarios described in docs/reference/architecture.md. The diff preserves those layer contracts: serialized checkpoint size is read in the parent after the worker exits, and no kernel/gitstore verification or fold implementation changes. Contract v3 and sample v2 are explicitly versioned measurement formats; contract-v2.json is byte-identical to main. I found no layer-contract change requiring an architecture-page amendment in this head.

Security: I examined the measurement inputs and authority boundaries. The parent accepts only bounded full lowercase hexadecimal Git object IDs before constructing the cat-file object/path argument; the worker's trust/signature/fold path is unchanged. No secret/signing-key handling, permission, production refusal limit or signature bypass is introduced by this diff. The false-pass path and unsupported evidence/provenance claims above remain assurance defects and prevent approval. This is directly assigned corrective evidence work under #20084, not a self-initiated delivery relying on an authority-bearing request chain to establish a new governing production limit. The candidate correctly separates planning targets from adopted commitments; do not convert the 60-second planning target into an adopted commitment while repairing it.

Simplification: consolidate the repeated common qualifications (two primary samples, a diagnostic, no percentile claim, and planning versus adopted targets) into one shared methods/interpretation passage, with short case-specific exceptions. Preserve the actual rows, historical heads and joint-versus-single-actor distinctions. The empty-case guard should stay at the selection/entry boundary without expanding this into a harness redesign.

Independent validation on cbc3b81b: go test ./cmd/gitseq-perf ./internal/perflane ./internal/perfscenario passed (1.933s, 0.380s, 2.754s); the opt-in TestWorkerLeavesCheckpointBytesToTheLaneParent integration test passed (1.591s); go test -count=1 ./internal/docset passed (53.628s). The five retained file SHA-256 values match the page; all 30 JSONL records equal evidence.samples, with 20 primaries and ten diagnostics, expected round/position and checkpoint-source classifications, matching trusted/result digests, and the published rounded latency values and two-sample distribution summaries. All 51 retained load samples range from 2.67 to 4.40. I did not rerun the 50,000/500,000 campaign, full suite, race suite, or the author's 28 mutants, and do not claim independently measured timing or a complete numeric re-audit of every historical lane. These results support retaining the measured campaign, subject to the corrections above.

Ordinary inherited staleness was visible and explicitly reconciled by #20084/#21875; I did not treat it as a reason to refile or to reopen the closed scale/memory lanes. I also read the subsequent finding #21876 and restart child #21877. The latter is separately queued after #20084 lands and the current promised work; it is not an inline optimization in this repair. The old outside-main candidate retirements do not change this exact reviewed source head. Publish a corrected exact-head artifact citing this finding and request fresh independent review. No approval or merge authorization is given here.
